feature: slash commands /undo and /redo (half-turn rewind with redo branch)
why: Fork-authored half-turn rewind. COMMAND_REGISTRY is the single source every consumer derives from (/help, CLI autocomplete, Telegram command menu, Slack mapping, gateway dispatch), so deleting the two CommandDef rows in a commands.py merge resolution removes /undo and /redo from EVERY surface at once with no import error and no test failure — the shipped undo tests exercise the engine, not the routing. The registry-level canary closes exactly that gap.

feature: slash command /branch (alias /fork) incl. Discord context-inheriting thread spawn
why: Session branching. On Discord /branch spawns a thread that inherits context while the parent channel keeps its own session; elsewhere it is a classic in-place switch. Two surfaces, one registry row, and the `fork` alias is documented in the slash-command reference — losing the alias is a silent UX regression that no existing test catches.

feature: slash command /merge (fold a branch summary into its parent session)
why: Idempotent, owner-guarded fold-back of a branched session into its parent; writes ~/.hermes/merges/*.md. gateway_only=True is a load-bearing CONTRACT, not decoration: /merge has no branch/parent thread to fold into on the CLI surface. A merge that drops the flag makes it appear in the CLI where it cannot work. The canary asserts the flag AND the asymmetry against /branch (which must stay CLI-available).

feature: slash command /fast (OpenAI Priority Processing / Anthropic Fast Mode toggle)
why: Per-session or --global priority-processing toggle. test_fast_command.py (41 tests) is cited by the 'route identity helpers' entry for a DIFFERENT reason (persisted route lookup), so the command's own registration and its normal|fast|status subcommand surface were unowned. The subcommands tuple is what makes the modes tab-completable — emptying it degrades the command silently.

feature: discord free-response channels: scalar coercion + quoted-bot-mention exemption
why: Two behaviors that live as small conditions inside a very large gating block in on_message. (1) SCALAR COERCION: YAML parses a bare `free_response_channels: 1491973769726791812` as an int; an isinstance(raw, str) guard silently returns an empty set, the channel stops being free-response, and the bot goes MUTE for every unmentioned message with no error anywhere. (2) QUOTED-MENTION EXEMPTION: free-response channels routinely quote other bots (migration notes, pasted transcripts); the fork answers anyway and only stays silent when the message LITERALLY STARTS WITH another bot's mention. Neutering it makes the bot fall silent on any message that happens to quote another agent. Pre-existing coverage (test_discord_allowed_channels.py) tests a REPLICATED helper, not the real adapter method — so the real method was untested. This canary calls the real method.

feature: telegram intake sentinel makes silent inbound update drops visible
why: PR #639 (fork/main 6cc7ca42ee). A user DM was fetched by the poller, offset-confirmed to Telegram (pending_update_count back to 0), and never reached any handler — gateway healthy throughout, ZERO log evidence, unattributable after the fact. An observation-only TypeHandler in group -1 sees every update before any filter/auth-prefilter/batching can discard it, giving per-update attribution plus WARNING-level gap detection with the exact missing update_id range. THE GROUP -1 PRIORITY IS THE WHOLE FEATURE: at group>=0 a handler can discard an update before the sentinel observes it, reopening the exact blind spot. Census: OUTSTANDING upstream. The complement canary locks the registration priority and the no-false-alarm rules (contiguous / first-update / duplicate+reordered) that the shipped file does not.

feature: cron refuses provably cross-vendor model/provider pairs at create/update time
why: PR #641 (fork/main HEAD de200ebbf5). A job pinned to model='gpt-5.6-sol' + provider='claude-apr' was accepted, persisted, then failed EVERY fire with an unretryable HTTP 400. Burned real scheduled jobs on 2026-08-19 and again 2026-08-29. Rule #20b promotes the post-hoc cron-config-lint check into a create/update-time admission gate. THE FAIL-OPEN HALF IS THE FRAGILE HALF: the vendor maps are prefix-based and deliberately incomplete, so an unknown model or provider MUST yield vendor None and NOT be flagged. A merge that 'improves' this into a fail-closed catalog starts refusing every legitimate job on an uncatalogued model. Both halves are asserted. Census: OUTSTANDING upstream.

feature: test hygiene: evict MagicMock telegram modules before the real-PTB polling suite
why: PR #640 (fork/main 640e57bd84). ~29 gateway unit-test files install a MagicMock under the telegram module names via sys.modules.setdefault so they can run without PTB. In a COMBINED run any of them executing first poisons this suite: importorskip finds the mock and 'succeeds', every telegram import binds MagicMock attributes, and all tests fail with "object MagicMock can't be used in await expression" — while passing in isolation. The fix evicts any telegram sys.modules entry whose __file__ is not a str, then reloads the adapter. NO CANARY BY DESIGN: asserting the helper exists would be a change-detector test (AGENTS.md: 'behavior contracts over snapshots'), and reproducing the pollution needs 29 mock-installing modules imported first. This entry exists so a merge reviewer knows the eviction block is LOAD-BEARING and must survive a tests/ resolution toward upstream — its absence produces an order-dependent flake invisible to CI slicing that happens to separate the files. Census: OUTSTANDING upstream.
coverage_gap: Deliberately no canary — self-guarding but only in a combined run. See `why`.

feature: gateway runtime footer fork fields: provider_model, context_full, reasoning
why: Census 2026-08-29: PR #80661 is still OUTSTANDING upstream (provider_model / context_full / reasoning are absent from upstream's gateway/runtime_footer.py) WHILE the sibling `latency` field from #71990 WAS ABSORBED via #77611. That makes this single file a live merge seam where upstream owns part and the fork owns the rest — the classic silent-drop shape: resolve toward upstream and the footer just renders shorter, no exception, no red test. Also locks the SKIP-SILENTLY doctrine (a field with missing data contributes nothing rather than '?%'), which is the byte-stability property upstream explicitly endorsed when absorbing the latency field on the same design — so keeping it is also what keeps #80661 landable.
